capabilities: Record vault, performance, and plugin metrics into a SQLite-backed local database
Render PromQL timeseries, stat, and table panels from code blocks in notes
Query the local database with a PromQL subset and pin dashboard time ranges
Expose an optional Prometheus-compatible HTTP API for tools like Grafana
Scrape external Prometheus endpoints into local history
disambiguation: Not a general database for note content; it stores time-series metrics only, with charts as the main user-facing output.
extras: The manifest warns the plugin has not been manually reviewed by Obsidian staff. The Prometheus HTTP server is disabled by default; local recording and note charting work without it.
problem: Obsidian has no built-in way to collect metrics over time, query them, or embed live charts of them in notes.

relations.evidence: TSDB exposes the familiar Prometheus metric types through prom-client
Grafana can use TSDB as a Prometheus datasource by pointing it at the bound base URL
TSDB can both expose a Prometheus-compatible server and scrape Prometheus endpoints
TSDB records metric samples into a SQLite database using wa-sqlite

requires.name: other Obsidian plugins that register metric stores

summary: Local time-series database that records vault and plugin metrics in SQLite and renders live PromQL chart panels in notes.
